learning_outcomes.text: The student will possess the fundamental knowledge required to analyze a chemical process and perform material balances involving chemical reactions.

The student will have knowledge on classical thermodynamics and the principles for evaluating the thermodynamic properties of pure substances, with particular emphasis on gaseous and liquid compounds.
The student will acquire fundamental knowledge regarding the thermodynamics of mixtures, as well as the tools to evaluate their properties and the equilibria of phases and reacting systems.
Select and apply the main equations of state to different fluids.
Determine the work and efficiency of different thermodynamic cycles.
Apply the main relationships to solve liquid-liquid and vapor-liquid equilibrium of multicomponent mixtures.

syllabus_topics: Chemical engineering: history, evolution and perspectives, specificity in the field of engineering.
Preliminary concepts and basic tools for the analysis of physical phenomena, the mathematical simulation of real systems and the validation of results.
Fundamental equations in terms of macroscopic balances with particular reference to the material balances with chemical reactions.
First and second principles of thermodynamics. Thermal machines and heat pumps. Combination of the first and second principles.
Volumetric behavior of pure fluids, state diagrams and tables, Equations of State (EoS).
Thermodynamics of pure fluids: thermodynamic functions, Maxwell relations, residual functions, Joule - Thomson coefficient.

Thermodynamics of phase equilibrium (Clausius-Clapeyron, Antoine). Fugacity and equilibrium conditions, calculation of fugacity with the equations of state and by indirect method for condensed phases.

Properties of mixtures, partial molar properties, Gibbs - Duhem equation. Perfect gas mixtures, real fluids-residual functions from EoS. (Coefficient of) Fugacity for a compound in a mixture and relationship with the residual Gibbs free energy.
Condensed phases. Ideal mixtures, non-ideal mixtures (excess functions). Activity coefficient models (Margules, van Laar, Wilson), NRTL, UNIQUAC and UNIFAC models.

Phases equilibrium in mixture. Gibbs phase rule. Equations for calculating equilibrium conditions. Vapor Liquid Equilibrium (Raoult's law), supercritical compounds, direct methods for high pressures. Liquid-liquid equilibrium (solubility diagrams), calculation at medium and low pressure. Vapor-Liquid-Liquid Equilibrium. Solid-liquid equilibrium. Dilute systems: freezing point depression, Boiling-point elevation, solubilities of a solute in two liquids, solubility of gases in liquids (Henry's law).

Systems with chemical reactions. Closed systems and open systems at stady-state, extent of reaction, equilibrium conditions, standard reference states. Influence of temperature on the equilibrium constant K. Heterogeneous systems with chemical reacions. Francis diagram. Non-stoichiometric method: the Gibbs free energy minimization method. Energy balance in multicomponent systems with chemical reactions.

Introduction to Aspen Plus, determination of the thermodynamic parameters of the various components of the software library, Plot of VLE diagrams, Equilibrium Reactor and Gibbs Reactor for the calculation of equilibrium compositions in reagent systems.
assessment_rules: The assessment includes a written test and an oral test during the exam sessions, each contributing 50% to the final grade. The written test consists of solving 3 exercises similar to those done in class. The oral test involves a discussion of the written exam and 2-3 additional questions to verify knowledge of thermodynamic concepts and application ability. Excellence is achieved if the student can solve unusual or unaddressed problems.
